News.title: Marburg Virus Disease
News.content:
Key facts

Marburg virus disease (MVD) is a severe, often fatal illness in humans

On average half of those who get the disease will die – although rates can be higher

Early supportive care with rehydration and symptomatic treatment improves survival

There are currently no approved vaccines or antiviral treatments for MVD, but a range of vaccines and drug therapies are under development

Overview

Marburg virus disease , formerly known as Marburg haemorrhagic fever, is a severe and often fatal illness in both humans and non-human primates. It is caused by the Marburg virus and Ravn virus, both of which are part of the Filoviridae family. It is closely linked to Ebola virus disease although it is a different virus. It is transmitted to humans from fruit bats and can spread from person to person.

Signs and symptoms

The incubation period for Marburg virus disease is typically between two to 21 days. The onset of the illness is abrupt and symptoms include.

Fever

Chills

Headache

Muscle aches

Rash with both flat and raised bumps, often on the torso

Chest pain

Sore throat

Nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea

Abdominal pain and cramping

Non-itchy rash

Dangers and complications

Marburg virus disease is a serious and deadly illness. In fatal cases, death often occurs between eight and nine days after the onset of symptoms.

As the disease advances, symptoms can become more severe. These can include liver failure, delirium, shock, bleeding (haemorrhaging), and multi-organ dysfunction. Some patients may develop fresh blood in vomit and faeces, as well as bleeding from the nose, gums, and vagina. Those affected can also be confused, irritable and aggressive.

It can be difficult to distinguish the disease from other infectious diseases such as malaria, typhoid and other haemorrhagic fevers such as Ebola.

Transmission

Marburg virus infection occurs via contact with the saliva, urine and faeces of the infected fruit bat, Rousettus aegyptiacus. Once the disease has spilled over from wildlife to people, the virus can spread through direct contact with the blood, secretions, organs or other bodily fluids of infected people, and with surfaces and materials contaminated with these fluids. This includes clothing, bedding, needles, and equipment.

Healthcare workers have frequently been infected while treating patients, particularly when infection control precautions are not strictly practiced. Burial ceremonies involving direct contact with the body of the deceased can also contribute to the transmission. The virus can also be sexually transmitted.

People cannot transmit the virus before they have symptoms but remain infectious as long as their blood contains the virus.

Treatment

Currently, there are no licenced treatments for Marburg, although some are in development. There has also been research showing potential with two antivirals. However, currently treatment is mainly limited to supportive care. This includes rest, hydration, managing oxygen status and blood pressure, and treatment of secondary infections.

Prevention

Scientists in Oxford are in the early stages of testing a vaccine against the disease. However, current prevention methods include:

Avoiding contact with blood and body fluids of people who are sick

Not handling items that may have come in contact with an infected person’s body fluids

Avoiding contact with fruit bats and non-human primates if in areas where Marburg is found

Ensuring all animal products (blood and meat) are thoroughly cooked before consumption

Isolating suspected or confirmed MVD patients in a designated treatment centre.

Ensuring safe burials

Identifying and monitoring people who have been in contact with infected individuals

History

Marburg virus disease was first recognised in 1967 after two simultaneous outbreaks in Marburg and Frankfurt in Germany, and in Belgrade, Serbia. These outbreaks were linked to laboratory work involving African green monkeys imported from Uganda. Since then, outbreaks and sporadic cases have been reported in several African countries, including Rwanda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, South Africa, Tanzania and Uganda.

The largest outbreak on record occurred in 2005 in Angola and involved 252 cases, of which 227 people died.

In 2008, two cases were reported in travellers – one from the US and the other from the Netherlands – who had visited a cave inhabited by Rousettus aegyptiacus bat colonies in Uganda.

In 2024 and 2025 Tanzania experienced an outbreak of the disease – although it was controlled all 10 people who were affected died.

News.title: Malaria
News.content:
Key facts

Malaria is a serious infection spread by mosquitoes, which can be deadly if not treated quickly

The disease is caused by a parasite transmitted through the bite of infected Anopheles mosquitoes

In 2023, there were an estimated 263 million cases and 597,000 deaths globally, with the majority of these in sub-Saharan Africa

Children under 5 are particularly vulnerable

Malaria is preventable and curable with the use of medicines and preventative measures.

Overview

Malaria is a life-threatening disease caused by the bite of a female Anopheles mosquito, infected with a parasite. The disease is very common in tropical regions, including large areas of Africa and Asia, Central and South America, and some Pacific islands. Malaria cannot be spread directly from person to person.

Malaria can range from a very mild illness to severe disease and even death. Starting treatment as soon as possible is imperative.

Signs and symptoms

Malaria symptoms can be difficult to spot as they are similar to other fevers. They may include high temperature, sweats and chills.

Dangers and complications

Malaria can be a deadly disease if not diagnosed and treated quickly. Untreated, malaria can cause severe illness or death within 24 hours. Infants, children under 5 years, pregnant women and girls, travellers (who have no immunity), and people with HIV or AIDS are at higher risk of severe infection. Malaria infection during pregnancy can also cause premature delivery or delivery of a baby with low birth weight. Malaria can sometimes return and require further treatment.

Severe symptoms are:

extreme tiredness and fatigue

impaired consciousness

multiple convulsions

difficulty breathing

dark or bloody urine

jaundice (yellowing of the eyes and skin)

abnormal bleeding.

Transmission

Malaria is caused by a parasite transmitted through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes. When an Anopheles mosquito bites a person with malaria, the mosquito becomes infectious. When this mosquito bites another person, it transmits the virus. Malaria is not spread from person to person like a cold or the flu, nor is it sexually transmitted.

Malaria can also be transmitted through blood transfusions and contaminated needles. The first symptoms of malaria may be mild and difficult to recognise, similar to many other febrile illnesses. P. falciparum is the deadliest malaria parasite, and is most prevalent in Africa. P. vivax is the dominant malaria parasite outside of sub-Saharan Africa.

Treatment

Malaria is considered an emergency and needs to be treated quickly with antimalarial medicines. Artemisinin-based combination therapy medicines are the most effective treatment for P. falciparum malaria. Chloroquine is recommended for treatment of infection with the P. vivax parasite only in places where it is still sensitive to this medicine. Antimalarial drug resistance is a growing problem and the World Health Organization urges regular monitoring of drug efficacy.

Prevention

Travellers to areas where the disease is endemic should take antimalarial medicine, starting a few days or weeks before you travel and continuing it when you return. However, the medication will not prevent all cases and avoiding getting bitten is important. Insect repellent should be used, and you should sleep under insecticide-treated mosquito nets. Wearing long-sleeved clothing and trousers in the evening, when mosquitoes are most active, can also help to prevent bites.

For people living in endemic regions, game changing vaccines are now being rolled out in routine childhood immunisation programmes across Africa – two different vaccines have now been shown to be effective.

Other prevention strategies for people living in malaria endemic countries include the use of insecticide treated bed nets, spraying inside homes and the use of chemoprophylaxis – where vulnerable populations are given antimalarial medication during times of the greatest malarial risk.

History

Malaria is one of the oldest diseases known to humanity, with some historians even arguing that it played a part in the fall of the Roman empire. Malaria flourished throughout the world, including in Britain where it was commonplace around the Thames marshes and was known as either marsh fever or ague.

There was huge progress against the disease in the 20th century and it was eradicated in Europe and the United States. In 2019 China was also officially declared free of the disease – a remarkable achievement for a country 90 per cent of whose population lived in malaria endemic areas in the 1940s.

Africa and south east Asia have also seen huge declines in the number of cases since the beginning of millennium thanks to renewed efforts to eradicate the disease. However, that progress has stalled in recent years: according to WHO’s World Malaria Report 2024 there were about 11 million more cases of the disease in 2023 than in 2022.

There is concern that malaria could easily come surging back due to a number of factors: drug resistance; the spread of a “super mosquito” from Asia to Africa; climate change leading to an explosion in mosquito numbers; and a drop in funding for control efforts. However, the roll out of two vaccines in recent years has provided a glimmer of hope.

News.title: Lassa Fever
News.content:
Key facts

Lassa fever is an acute viral illness caused by the Lassa virus

The disease is spread to humans primarily through contact with infected rodents or items contaminated with their urine and faeces

Person-to-person transmission can occur, especially in hospitals or clinics where there is poor infection control

Most people infected with Lassa virus experience mild symptoms, but the disease can be severe or fatal

Lassa fever is endemic in parts of west Africa

Overview

Lassa fever is an acute viral haemorrhagic illness that comes on quickly after infection. The Lassa virus, which causes the fever, belongs to the Arenaviridae virus family. The disease was first identified in 1969 in Nigeria, but has also been found in Benin, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Mali and Sierra Leone.

Lassa fever is a zoonotic disease, meaning that it spreads from animals to humans. The main animal reservoir for the virus is the multimammate rat (Mastomys natalensis), which is common throughout sub-Saharan Africa. These rats do not get sick from the virus but shed it in their urine and faeces.

Signs and symptoms

About 80 per cent of those who are infected display no symptoms but for those who do become ill the onset of Lassa fever is usually gradual, with symptoms appearing one to three weeks after infection.

Mild symptoms may include:

Slight fever

Fatigue and weakness

Headache

Sore throat

Generalised pain

Lassa fever can be hard to diagnose as the symptoms are varied and similar to diseases such as Ebola, typhoid and malaria.

Dangers and complications

Some people develop severe disease, with the virus affecting organs such as the liver, spleen and kidneys. Lassa fever is fatal in about one per cent of cases – among those who are hospitalised around 15 per cent will die. Other complications include hearing loss, with around a quarter of recovered patients with some level of deafness, which can be permanent. The disease is particularly dangerous in pregnancy with maternal death and or foetal loss in around 80 per cent of cases.

In more severe cases, additional symptoms can include:

Bleeding

Difficulty breathing

Vomiting

Facial swelling

Bleeding from the mouth, nose, vagina or gastrointestinal tract

Chest, back and abdominal pain

Neurological impairment

Transmission

The main way to contract Lassa fever is through contact with food or household items contaminated by the urine or faeces of infected rats, that is by eating contaminated food, touching contaminated objects, or breathing in air contaminated with the virus. The virus can also enter through open cuts or sores. Infection can also occur through direct contact with infected rats.

Person-to-person transmission can occur through contact with bodily fluids, such as blood, urine, faeces or semen of an infected person. This is more common in healthcare settings, where the virus can spread via medical equipment.

Treatment

The antiviral drug ribavirin has been used to treat Lassa fever, although the evidence for its effectiveness is still under debate. Other antiviral treatments are in development. Supportive care is crucial for improving survival rates, this includes: rehydration and management of symptoms such as vomiting, diarrhoea, fever and pain. Blood transfusions, dialysis, and ventilation may also be necessary in severe cases.

Prevention

Preventing Lassa fever involves controlling rodent populations and avoiding contact with rodents and their excreta. In endemic areas, it’s important to:

Store food in rat-proof containers

Maintain a clean household

Dispose of garbage far from the home

Avoid eating rodents

Trap rats in and around homes

People should also avoid contact with the blood and body fluids of infected individuals, as well as contaminated items like bedding.

The non-profit vaccine developer IAVI launched the first ever phase II trial of a vaccine against the disease across three sites in Ghana, Liberia and Nigeria in 2024.

History

Lassa fever was first documented in 1969, with the first cases occurring in Lassa, Nigeria. About 300,000 people fall ill with the disease across West Africa every year although the true number of cases is thought to be much higher. Between 1971 and 2024 there have been 16 cases in the UK – all linked to travel to the region.

Climate change and population growth have forced humans and the rodents that carry the disease into closer contact. The WHO has classified Lassa fever as an epidemic threat that requires urgent action in terms of developing vaccines and treatments.

News.title: Human Papillomavirus (HPV)
News.content:
Key facts

Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the name of a group of 200 viruses – while most are harmless some high-risk HPV types are linked to cancer

Almost all cervical cancers are linked to HPV

HPV is primarily spread through skin-to-skin contact, often during sexual activity.

In 2019, HPV caused an estimated 620,000 cancer cases in women and 70 000 cancer cases in men.

Vaccination against HPV can prevent these cancers

Overview

HPV is a common sexually transmitted infection (STI). Most sexually active people will be infected at some point in their lives, often without experiencing any symptoms. In most cases, the body’s immune system clears the virus on its own. HPV can affect the skin, genital area, and throat.

However, HPV can lead to the development of cancers – according to the World Health Organization 99 per cent of all cervical cancers are linked to the virus. A vaccine is now available against HPV – in countries where immunisation is well established, it has led to a huge decrease in the incidence of cervical cancer.

Signs and symptoms

Most people with HPV do not develop any symptoms or health problems. In many cases, the infection will resolve itself without the person ever knowing they had it. However, some people may experience symptoms that can include:

Genital warts, which may appear as small bumps or groups of bumps in the genital area. These warts can vary in size and shape.

Unusual growths or lumps in the genital area, mouth, or throat.

Sores in the genital area, mouth, or throat.

Early changes to cervical cells that can only be detected through screening

Symptoms of cervical cancer such as bleeding between periods or after sexual intercourse or a foul-smelling vaginal discharge.

Dangers and complications

Most of the time HPV does not cause any problems. However, in some people, certain types of HPV can cause genital warts or abnormal changes in cells that may sometimes turn into cancer. High-risk types of HPV are linked to various cancers including:

Cervical cancer: the most common type of cancer caused by HPV.

Anal cancer

Penile cancer

Vulval cancer

Vaginal cancer

Some types of head and neck cancers including at the back of the throat, base of the tongue, and tonsils.

Cancers often take many years, even decades, to develop after a person gets HPV. People with weakened immune systems may be more likely to develop health problems from HPV.

Transmission

HPV is primarily spread through skin-to-skin contact of the genital area. It can be transmitted through any skin-to-skin contact in the genital area. Ways HPV can be spread includes:

Vaginal, anal, or oral sex.

Sharing sex toys.

Close skin-to-skin touching during sex.

A person with HPV can pass the infection to someone else even when they have no signs or symptoms. You do not need to have sex with a lot of people to get HPV. You can get HPV the first time you have sex.

Treatment

There is no treatment for the HPV virus itself. Most HPV infections do not cause any problems and are cleared by the body on its own within two years. However, there are treatments available for health problems that HPV can cause, such as:

Genital warts can be treated with prescription medicine or by a healthcare provider.

Cervical precancer can be treated if found through routine Pap tests.

Cancers caused by HPV are more treatable when found and treated early.

Prevention

There are ways to lower your chances of getting HPV and avoid the health problems it can cause:

HPV vaccination: the HPV vaccine is safe and effective, and it protects against the types of HPV that cause most cases of genital warts and cervical cancer, as well as some other cancers. It is most effective when given before a person is exposed to the virus – in the UK it is given to boys and girls from the age of 12 and 13

Routine cervical screening for women aged 25 to 64 can help protect against cervical cancer by detecting precancerous cell changes before they become cancer

Using condoms

Avoiding sex when you have genital warts: If you or your partner have genital warts, stop having sex until the warts are gone.

Voluntary male circumcision

Being a non-smoker or stopping smoking reduces the chances of developing a persistent HPV infection.

History

The link between HPV and cervical cancer was first recognised in the 1980s when scientists studied the cells of Henrietta Lacks, an African American woman who died of cervical cancer in 1951. Her cells, named HeLa, were the first sign that cancer could be caused by a virus.

German virologist Harald zur Hausen identified HPV DNA in cervical cancer biopsies, which led to the development of the HPV vaccine. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 2008 for his discovery.

Vaccination against the virus has been a remarkable success story. The first HPV vaccine was approved in 2006 and in 2008 vaccination was rolled out for girls in the UK. A 2024 study led by scientists at Cancer Research UK and St Mary’s University, London found that the vaccination programme had cut the number of cervical cases by 90 per cent in England. A study in the Lancet in 2018 showed that Australia is on track to be the first country to eliminate cervical cancer if its vaccination and screening programme continue at the same rate.

News.title: Britain’s £8bn bet on the developing world
News.content:
Britain will invest up to £8bn in companies across the developing world over the next five years, in a bid to make a return for the UK taxpayer while driving global development.

The initiative is being led by British International Investment (BII), a government owned UK investment vehicle founded in 1948 to boost agricultural production across the empire.

At the time, Britain faced food shortages and rationing in the wake of the Second World War.

Jenny Chapman, the UK Minister for Development, now wants to accelerate the flow of capital to developing countries via BII as UK overseas direct aid budgets are shrinking.

It is envisaged that for every pound of public money BII invests a matched contribution will come from the private sector, bringing the total investment to about £15 billion.

Leslie Maasdorp, the South Africa born Chief Executive of BII, said: “Britain has a proud history of acting as a global leader in international development. BII is committed to demonstrating that a new, mutually-beneficial path exists that creates secure jobs and stable economic conditions in the countries in which we invest, while providing value for money for the UK taxpayer”.

Investing in developing economies is high risk but can also bring in substantial financial rewards beyond the help it provides locally in terms of innovation and jobs.

Over the last decade, BII generated a £1.6 billion return on investments, equating to a return of around five per cent a year. The new five year cycle envisages a minimum return on capital of at least two per cent but managers will be hoping for more.

The fund’s capital will also support UK based companies that are delivering positive economic and environmental outcomes in developing markets.

In an interview with the Telegraph, Mr Maasdorp said that development and national security were “reinforcing” concepts and “not opposites”.

News.title: Tired Man City inch to the top and send Burnley back to Championship
News.content:
Manchester City have not been top of the Premier League since the opening weekend of the season but they will usurp Arsenal at the summit tonight with a win at Burnley.

Victory would put City top courtesy of a superior goal difference if they win by two goals or more, or on goals scored if they win by just the one.

The more realistic Arsenal fans tuning into watch will be hoping Burnley, who will be relegated by a City win at Turf Moor this evening, can simply keep the score down.

City’s 2-1 victory over Arsenal in Sunday’s entertaining duel between the country’s two best teams means the title race is now in their hands and could go to the wire.

Technically speaking, it is in Arsenal’s hands too because the two teams will be level on points and close enough on goal difference, but that measure should favour a City team full of firepower.

They have found form and tactical balance at just the right time: Marc Guehi has settled into the heart of their defence, Nico O’Reilly is flying at left-back, Rodri and Bernardo Silva are rolling back the years in midfield and an awesome foursome of Antoine Semenyo, Rayan Cherki, Jeremy Doku and Erling Haaland leads the attack.

The expectation is that City will reel off six more wins on their way to a seventh league title under Pep Guardiola while Arsenal fall away, but both contenders still have a lot of football to play.

Burnley lost 2-0 to Arsenal, 1-0 to Liverpool and drew 2-2 with Manchester United at Turf Moore, so Scott Parker’s team have been relatively competitive against the big teams at home, but this is an even harder task.

It is an unlikely outcome, but the title could be decided by goal difference so City will not relent should they get in front tonight. Rodri misses the game with a groin injury.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Bat coronavirus develops new ways to infect humans, says study
News.content:
The discovery came after scientists set out to better understand and characterise the spike proteins in alphacoronavirus. Unlike betacoronaviruses – which include Sars-Cov-2 – there has been little research into alphacoronaviruses.

The scientists began by identifying some 2,000 coronavirus virus sequences that had already been published in a public database called Genbank. Next, they used a computational approach to narrow this down to 40 spike proteins that reflect alphacoronaviruses’ genetic diversity.

The spikes were incorporated into lab-safe pseudoviruses, then tested against libraries of known coronavirus receptors from different species. The vast majority did not have receptor binding domains that could infect people – CcCoV-KY43 was the one exception.

“What is very nice about this elegant work is that all the discoveries were made without the need to work with any dangerous viruses,” said Prof Wendy Barclay, a professor of infectious disease at Imperial College London, who was not involved in the study.

“The scientists used a state of the art approach taking sequences derived from the original bat samples in Kenya to recreate surrogates that mimic the virus but are not infectious to humans. The use of a platform to scan a huge range of potential human receptors is also a big advance here.”

‘Not a new Covid-19’

The researchers said the work also provides a blueprint for identifying and preparing for a potential spillover event before it emerges – blood samples taken in southeastern Kenya suggest people have not been exposed to the virus. In the past, receptor binding domains have been studied only after a virus has jumped into people.

“This is not a new Covid-19, there are many steps after entry that are needed for a virus to be able to replicate in the human cell, and then release [and spread],” Dr Dalan Bailey, a specialist in the molecular biology of RNA viruses at The Pirbright Institute, told a briefing.

“We don’t have evidence that this virus has spilled into human populations in Kenya, but we’re now in a much better position to start preparing for that potential risk,” he added. “Outbreak prevention starts with understanding risk.”

Prof Stuart Neil, head of the Department of Infectious Diseases at King’s College London and not involved in the research, said it was an interesting study that highlights “the incredible plasticity in these viruses and why we need to keep an eye on them”.

But he added that there are still more questions to answer to fully understand the risk – including whether CcCoV-KY43 can actually replicate and grow inside humans, and whether it has jumped from bats to other local mammals in Kenya.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez wanted by Chelsea’s Premier League rivals in shock transfer twist as Real Madrid joined in race
Sports.content:
ENZ-WOAH Enzo Fernandez wanted by Chelsea’s Premier League rivals in shock transfer twist as Real Madrid joined in race

MANCHESTER CITY are weighing up a shock move for Enzo Fernandez.

The Argentine midfielder made the move to Chelsea for a then-British-record fee of £105million in 2023.



But speculation has grown that he could be on the way out of Stamford Bridge amid a nightmare season for the Blues that saw boss Liam Rosenior sacked on Wednesday.



The Athletic report that early interest is materialising in the midfielder’s services, and he is one of a collection of names being monitored for the summer window.

The North West club are joining Spanish giants Real Madrid in the hunt for the 25-year-olds services.

Fernandez recently served a two-match suspension handed down by the Chelsea hierarchy after hinting at a summer exit to Los Blancos.

Just days after refusing to rule out a summer exit, Fernandez revealed ina YouTube video: “I’d like to live in Madrid. It’s a beautiful city, reminds me of Buenos Aires.”

Sports.title: Liverpool title hero ‘lined up by Premier League rivals as he plots Anfield exit this summer’
Sports.content:
TWO Premier League sides are primed to battle it out for Curtis Jones this summer, according to reports.

The Liverpool midfielder, 25, is frustrated by a lack of game time under Arne Slot this season.



He has played 44 games in all competitions but only 13 of those were Premier League starts.



And Jones is now ‘strongly considering’ a move away from Merseyside, where he has been on the books since age nine.

According to talkSPORT, Aston Villa and Tottenham would be two eager customers if Jones decides to call it quits.

Villa are said to have added the England international to their list of summer transfer targets.

And Spurs ‘would be keen’ to try their luck if they manage to beat the drop under Roberto De Zerbi.



Those two sides could also face competition from abroad after Inter Milan courted Jones during the January window.

Jones has scored 21 goals in 223 Liverpool games and won two Premier League titles, three domestic cups and a Champions League since making his debut in 2019.

He has only ever played for the Reds, with previous boss Jurgen Klopp and current manager Slot opting to keep him in and around the first team.

And his exploits at club level have seen him turn out six times for England, scoring once.

It is possible that a change of manager could convince Jones to give his Liverpool career another chance.

But, despite becoming unpopular with large sections of the fanbase, Slot is believed to retain the backing of the Reds board.



Jones only has one year remaining on his contract, so this summer would be the most logical time for Liverpool to sell, unless they plan to offer him an extension.

Sports.title: Arsenal files: Arteta revives transfer interest amid Ben White doubts, Dowman and boss’ video messages
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are tracking Sporting defender Ivan Fresneda as they look to sign a new full-back this summer.

The Gunners are keeping tabs on several targets and also hold an interest in Newcastle’s Tino Livramento.



Celta Vigo defender Oscar Mingueza is another player they have scouted and is an attractive option as his contract expires at the end of this season.



Arsenal’s interest in Fresneda dates back to January 2023, when he was playing for Valladolid in Spain.

The right-back, 21, ended up joining Sporting that summer for around £8million – but Arsenal are now tracking him again.

Fresneda has a release clause in his current contract that is worth €80m (£69m), but it is thought he could be sold for less than that.

The defender will have two years left on his deal this summer and Sporting are tempted to cash in on him.



The arrival of a new full-back at Arsenal would raise doubts over the future of Ben White.

The right-back has only started 18 games this season and was on the bench for both of last week’s huge clashes with Sporting and Man City.

White, 28, will have two years left on his contract at the end of this season and has been linked with a move to Everton.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Full Arsenal on YouTube SunSport have launched a dedicated Arsenal channel on YouTube! The Full Arsenal Podcast is your home for everything about the Gunners. From match reactions and tactical breakdowns to transfer talk, match previews, tactical analysis and honest fan debate… The Full Arsenal covers it all. Subscribe to The Full Arsenal here

VID KIDS

ARSENAL’S UNDER-15s received video messages of support from Mikel Arteta and a host of first-team players ahead of the Next Gen Beijing Cup final.



The Young Guns beat Zhejiang Professional 2-0 in the final to lift the trophy without conceding a single goal.

Ahead of that showdown, the rising stars were shown video messages wishing them luck from Arsenal boss Arteta and three former Hale End academy stars.

Max Dowman, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Eberechi Eze all passed on some words of encouragement to the teenagers.

Players were also given the chance to have a 45-minute Q&A with academy chief Per Mertesacker, who offered career advice and spoke about his biggest achievements in the game.



The tour was the last for Mertesacker, who announced in January that he would be leaving the club at the end the season following eight years shaping the future stars of N5.

GEOR THE ONE

ARSENAL are confident of kicking off a big summer for their women’s side by signing England star Georgia Stanway and Spain full-back Ona Batlle.

The pair are both out of contract at the end of this season and the Gunners plan to get their key transfer business done early this summer.

The signing of England midfielder Stanway, 27, would be a major coup and underline Arsenal’s desire to win the Women’s Super League next season.



They last lifted the WSL back in 2019 and are currently third, with leaders City 11 points clear of them having played two games more.

Stanway is ready to leave Bayern Munich and return to England, with Arsenal the clear frontrunners to sign her.

They are also in pole position to bring in Batlle, who is set to leave Barcelona on a free transfer this summer.

The Spain star spent three years in England with Manchester United from 2020 to 2023 before returning to her childhood club, Barca.

Batlle is eager to have another crack at playing in the WSL and Arsenal want to sign a full-back as Katie McCabe is leaving.



Arsenal bolstered the recruitment department of their women’s team in January by appointing Jodie Taylor as their technical director.

The former England striker works alongside director of women’s football, Clare Wheatley, and the pair have been pushing hard to nail down summer signings early.

FOOD FOR THOUGHT

FANS heading to the Emirates next season can expect a big change as the stadium is set to have a new food and drink supplier.

Delaware North have provided food and drink at the Emirates since it opened in 2006 after striking a 20-year deal with Arsenal back then.



But the contract expires this summer and SunSport understands that the Gunners will be going with a new supplier next season.

That should mean a boost to Arsenal’s finances as SunSport reported last year how a new deal could be worth at least £500,000 PER GAME in revenue.

The Gunners struck a long-term deal with Delaware North in 2006 and it was a wise move at a time when the club was short on cash.

The club previously tried to buy themselves out of the deal, though, and will part ways with Delaware North this summer.

NO MAR THAN THAT

MARLI SALMON’S new contract will tie him down until August 2029 at the latest.



Arsenal announced this week that Salmon has signed a pre-contract agreement with the club that will see him ink his first pro deal on his 17th birthday.

FA rules dictate that 17-year-olds cannot sign contracts any longer than three years, meaning Salmon is unable to commit his long-term future to the club beyond 2029.

That period of three years will start from the day Salmon turns 17 on August 29.

Max Dowman is also caught in the same situation, having agreed a pre-contract ahead of his 17th birthday on December 31.



Once a payer turns 18, there is no restriction on the length of the deal they can sign.

It is commonplace for a new lucrative five-year contract to be put on the table the week that a player turns 18, even though two years remain on their first pro deal.

EYES ON THE PRIZE

MANCHESTER CITY and Arsenal’s title clash last weekend was the most-watched Premier League match in US history.

That is according to research from the official Nielsen Big Data + Panel and digital data from Adobe Analytics.



City’s 2-1 win over the Gunners averaged 2.6m viewers across NBC, Peacock, Telemundo and NBC Sports Digital platforms.

That is a new record for a Prem game and the US has enjoyed bumper viewing figures this season.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Arsenal’s trip to Manchester United in August had 2.5m viewers, making it the third most-watched Prem game in US history.

The promising figures bode well ahead of this summer’s World Cup in Canada, Mexico and the US.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo teammate hurls water bottle in pitch-side meltdown at his OWN manager as players forced to intervene
Sports.content:
INIGO MARTINEZ threw a tantrum at boss Jorge Jesus as Al-Nassr booked their place in the Asian Champions League Two final.

Al-Nassr levelled within two minutes, and went on to win 5-1 courtesy of a Kingsley Coman hat-trick, in addition to strikes by Angelo Gabriel and Abdullah Al-Hamdan.

Despite his side’s dominant victory, Martinez found himself engaged in a touchline spat with Jesus as his team-mates celebrated a goal.

Martinez, 34, then viciously threw a water bottle at the ground, with it skidding in the direction of his boss.

The former Spain international signed for Al-Nassr as a free agent last summer after leaving Barcelona.

He has since made 37 appearances in all competitions, scoring four times.

Jesus, meanwhile, took over last summer after departing league rivals Al-Hilal.

Sports.title: Amazing moment goalkeeper scores brilliant equaliser in final minute of injury time to spark wild celebrations
Sports.content:
TORONTO goalkeeper Luka Gavran netted a dramatic stoppage-time equaliser for the MLS side to snatch a 3-3 draw against Philadelphia Union.

The Canadian shot-stopper had gone up for a late free kick as the game went past its additional five minutes of added time.





And he was unmarked to nod a glancing header into the back of the net to spark wild scenes inside the stadium.

Gavran wheeled away before performing a knee slide and was then mobbed by his delighted Toronto team-mates.

There was mayhem in the stands after what was the last action of the game to secure a vital point.

Even the commentator on Apple TV was stunned as he cried: “The keeper has levelled the game! It’s three!



“Look at Gavran, the hero, as they load the box! Who said they won’t settle for a draw? Are you kidding me?”

Fans were thrilled by the stunning moment as they hailed Gavran’s late heroics.

One wrote on X: “Saw this live at the stadium. Insane.”

A second added: “Limbs in the stands for this one omg, what a moment.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

A third wrote: “Well we don’t see this every day… Luka Gavran making history in the MLS.”

A fourth said: “MLS games going crazy, absolute scenes.”

Another claimed he “had his Alisson moment”, referencing the Liverpool goalkeepers’ dramatic winner against West Brom in 2021.



Former Norwich City star Josh Sargent had equalised for Toronto after Milan Iloski’s opener before Danley Jean Jacques put Philadelphia ahead again.

Kobe Franklin then levelled for Toronto once more before Nathan Harriel made it 3-2 in the 89th minute. Just eight minutes later Gavran had the last laugh in the fifth minute of stoppage time.

Gavran admitted the crazy scenes were almost a blur as he pointed out he used to be a striker.

Speaking to MLS 360, he said: “I can’t even remember what happened.

“I thought there were ten seconds left. I looked to the bench, and everyone was waving me down to go, so I was like, you know what?



“And then here, I thought [the referee] was going to blow [the whistle]. I was like, ‘OK, recycle my run’, and the rest was [history]… I used to be a No. 9, you know.

“We do set pieces every day, so you know I’m used to it. We had the team talk and I couldn’t even look at my phone; it was blowing up.

“Everyone’s messaging me and then it was like, ‘Oh, you got some interviews,’ so I’m still [buzzing] inside.”

Sports.title: Crazy moment football fan grabs TV camera mid-match and broadcasts his own FACE leaving viewers stunned
Sports.content:
THIS IS the bizarre moment a footie fan hijacked a TV camera mid-match to broadcast his OWN FACE.

The instinctive supporter took his chance just 36 minutes into a Copa Argentina clash between Acassuso and Gimnasia LP.





Footage broadcast to viewers live on TyC Sports turned rocky as the camera was first grabbed by the mystery man.

With Gimnasia launching a rapid counter-attack, the picture failed to follow the ball up the pitch.

Instead, the lens began to shake violently before tilting up to show the stands rather than the action on the grass.

Then, after a few seconds of chaos, the camera turned around fully to reveal a bloke’s face at point-blank range.



Smiling and shouting into the lens, the bald fanatic looked overjoyed to have caused such a scene.

The embarrassed TV director quickly cut to a pitch-level view from behind one of the goals to hide the disruption.

Rather than the standard horizontal view, the back-up camera tracked the ball while the cheeky intruder was dealt with.

The man was still in shot for around five seconds and seemed to have control of the camera for 10 seconds before it was dealt with.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Baffled fans online weren’t sure what to make of the stunt, with one fuming on X: “Now all the idiots are gonna start doing the same thing.”

Another joked: “It’s the most Copa Argentina sequence I’ve ever seen in my life.”

A third wrote: “Only in Argentine football do these things happen”.

While one fan added: “It reminded me of Heath Ledger’s Joker when he grabs the camera with the fake Batman.”

With the score still at 0-0 in this cup game, nothing much was missed.



Gimnasia eventually cruised to a 3-0 victory, with all three goals coming in a dominant second-half display.

The bald fan was reportedly escorted from the ground by security following his ten seconds of fame.

Sports.title: Women’s football coach suspended after telling player to join OnlyFans & threatening to ‘spank’ those who miss training
Sports.content:
CREEP COACH Women’s football coach suspended after telling player to join OnlyFans & threatening to ‘spank’ those who miss training

A COACH has been suspended after telling a female footballer to create an OnlyFans account.

Filipe Linz, a coach with Guia FC, was slammed with a one-year suspension by the Portuguese Football Federation amid a series of sexual harassment and discrimination allegations from multiple players.





He is alleged to have texted one of them on WhatsApp: “It’s always better than going to the roundabout, I would subscribe.”

The “roundabout” is believed to be a reference to an area in the coastal city of Albufeira, which is known for street prostitution.

“Today you were going to take a shower with me, but now you are not,” a message to another player read.

Other alleged messages to teammates read, “I dreamed about you.”

Linz also made suggestive comments about fathering a child with one of the footballers.

Evidence presented during the case launched by the Federation’s Disciplinary Council included highly inappropriate texts to at least six different Guia FC players.

He also allegedly told the women that they would be “spanked on the buttocks” or “hit on the hand” for missing training.

His comments about OnlyFans “call into question the sexual objectification and commercialisation of the victim,” the prosecution said.



The string of incidents happened between the 2020/21 and 2024/25 seasons.

Despite complaints, Guia FC’s management reportedly dismissed these as “jokes”.

Meanwhile, Linz claimed his messages were “taken out of context” and indicated he may pursue defamation charges against his accusers.

The Federation’s Disciplinary Council found that Linz engaged in a pattern of inappropriate behaviour.

He has been suspended for one year and 15 days alongside a fine of £866.



He is continuing to serve the club as a coach for the men’s side until his recent suspension.

Guia FC has also been penalised for failing to act on the initial complaints.

It will have to play two games behind closed doors and must pay a fine of £1,767.

Sports.title: Man Utd’s sexiest fan stuns in saucy mirror selfie as she wears rarely-seen Red Devils kit
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED’s sexiest fan Therese Gudmundsen has rocked the club’s third shirt in a mirror selfie.

Posing for a pic, Gudmundsen, who appears to still be on her travels, was kitted out in the stunning black top.





With the retro Adidas logo in yellow and a border around the badge, it is an instant classic for many.

And blonde favourite Gudmundsen pulled it off with matching yellow short leggings.

She tilted her hips in the snap posted to her Instagram story, covering her face.

Gudmundsen stood in the kitchen before later getting changed for something to eat – perhaps in a bid to avoid getting her United top dirty..

Her next upload was in a busty black top and unbuttoned white shirt.

Eating some watermelon, the United influencer wore sunglasses and a black headband outside.



She also had on a gold necklace.

Earlier in the day Gudmundsen showed off her piercing green-blue eyes in another selfie.

The Norwegian has over 325,000 followers on Insta and regularly lets fans take a glimpse into her daily life.

She has recently put up photos in retro United kits from the 90s with Eric Cantona‘s name on the back as well as a mid-2000s version with Cristiano Ronaldo on.

As she travels the world and takes holiday in Vietnam, Sri Lanka, and Indonesia, fans have been loving her updates.



Gudmundsen has a massive collection of United jerseys, also wearing a long-sleeved 2023-24 one outside Old Trafford last year.

She has a Ronaldo one for Portugal as well.

Sports.title: Roy Keane issues brutal Man Utd verdict in Bruno Fernandes debate: “Really low standards”
Sports.content:
Roy Keane issues brutal Man Utd verdict in Bruno Fernandes debate: “Really low standards”

Roy Keane has delivered a blunt reality check regarding talk of Bruno Fernandes as the PFA Player of the Year, citing Manchester United's standards as an issue

View 2 Images Roy Keane issued Gary Neville with a reality check regarding Man Utd and Bruno Fernandes (Image: Stick to Football)

Roy Keane has hit back at Gary Neville and claimed that Bruno Fernandes is only being talked up as a potential PFA Player of the Year because Manchester United's standards are "really, really low".

‌



The Portuguese star has long been the standout individual at Old Trafford and has enjoyed one of his best seasons to date. His numbers, especially in terms of creating chances and providing assists, set him apart from other players in the Premier League.

‌



As a result he's being talked up for individual accolades come the season's end. He is among the favourites to scoop the main award with Declan Rice, Erling Haaland and Bernardo Silva also in contention.

‌



Neville admits that Fernandes would get his pick, but feels as though the nostalgia surrounding Bernardo in his last season could see him land more votes. Keane equally felt the City midfielder would get it, especially if Pep Guardiola's side end up winning the domestic treble.

Man Utd ready to rival Liverpool in transfer race for Tottenham star Micky van de Ven READ MORE :

When Neville put forward his case for Fernandes he said on Stick to Football: "I just think where United are from where they've been all season." Keane then asked where they were, sarcastically saying "amazing" when Neville said third.

The Irishman, who drove standards when he was captain on the red side of Manchester, believed that Fernandes was benefiting in a team that had minimal expectation. He said: "But when your standards are really, really low and you go up a little bit.."

‌



Fernandes has been named the Sir Matt Busby Player of the Year on four occasions - the joint most of any player in United's history. He's also won the Premier League's Player of the Month award six times - only one shy of the record held by the likes of Mohamed Salah and Harry Kane.

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes is enjoying one of his best individual seasons to date (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Despite those individual awards Fernandes has won just two honours since moving to Manchester in January 2020. The playmaker has landed the Carabao Cup and the FA Cup, but never been part of a side that have challenged for the league, which he knows is the ultimate expectation.

Article continues below

He recently told the Telegraph: "So, the main thing that the club understood is this: it’s 2013 that they last won the Premier League. That’s too long for a club like Man United. Being now so long without winning a Premier League is not normal. As a player, you have to understand that the fans, the expectation, will always be that we want to come back and win the Premier League."

Sports.title: World Cup 2026: Brazil – Carlo Ancelotti gamble and why 'cursed' Selecao must win ugly
Sports.content:
For over two decades, the yellow shirt of Brazil has carried a weight that feels increasingly heavy. It's been 24 years since Ronaldo's shorn head and clinical finishing delivered the Seleção's fifth World Cup title in Yokohama and for a nation that views second place as "the first of the losers," the drought is becoming unbearable.

Brazil head into the 2026 World Cup as the ultimate sleeping giant - a team defined by a glorious, dazzling past but haunted by a pragmatic, frustrating present. Having failed to progress beyond the quarter-final stage since their 2002 triumph, the quest for the Hexa (the sixth title) has never felt more daunting.

At the heart of this struggle lies a fundamental identity crisis. The free-flowing flair and individual brilliance that once allowed Brazil to sweep teams aside now feel increasingly obsolete in a modern footballing landscape defined by hyper-structured, collectivist systems.

To turn the tide, the Brazilian FA has made a historic move, appointing their first foreign manager in over 60 years. They haven't just hired anyone; they've hired serial winner and cup competition extraordinaire Carlo Ancelotti - a man now tasked with restoring the world's most iconic footballing nation to its former glory.

‌



To understand the mood in Rio and São Paulo ahead of this summer's showpiece, we spoke to veteran commentator and author Jon Cotterill in the latest episode of Mirror Football's Make Football Great Again podcast. Based in Brazil for years, Cotterill provides an unfiltered perspective on the reality of 'modern' Brazilian football, why the Ancelotti appointment is a gamble and why a nation once obsessed with flair is now ready to win ugly.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The death of 'Joga Bonito'

For fans expecting a carnival of flamboyancy this summer, Cotterill has a reality check: Joga Bonito ['the Beautiful Game' - often used a synonym for Brazilian flair] is dead. The idea of Brazil as a team of dancing magicians is, in his view, a product of clever TV editing and deep nostalgia.

"I'm sorry to tell you, but it died decades ago," Cotterill admits. "People watch Brazil every four years and the TV companies drag out images from 50 years ago. The reality is a lot more pragmatic."

‌



He traces this shift back as far as 1966, noting that even the celebrated winners of 1994 and 2002 were built on steel rather than silk. "1994 was pretty grim - the final against Italy was an awful 0-0 draw. 2002 was under [Luis Felipe] Scolari and was very pragmatic," Cotterill adds.

"The 'Beautiful Game' has been buried for decades, though the squad they have now is arguably the best they've had since 1970."

View 5 Images Brazil will be one of the favourites heading into the tournament (Image: Getty Images)

End of the Neymar era

Perhaps the biggest shock from within the Brazilian camp is the total decline of their long-time poster boy and all-time goalscorer Neymar. For Cotterill, the chances of the former Barcelona and PSG superstar, now 34, making a meaningful impact - or even the squad - are non-existent.

‌



"The days of depending on Neymar are long over. There's absolutely no chance [he goes to the World Cup]. He's 34, he's been injured and he looks completely out of shape. I saw him recently and he looked like someone who had just played a Sunday League game.

"Under a Brazilian coach, politics might have got him in, but under Ancelotti, I don't think there's any chance. He’d be in danger of embarrassing himself against elite players."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

New heroes and 'next big thing'

With Neymar out of the picture, Brazil are looking for a new talisman. While Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior is the global star, Cotterill points to Barcelona's Raphinha as a key figure - albeit a volatile one.

‌



View 5 Images Vinicius Junior and Raphinha will lead Brazil's attack this summer (Image: Getty Images)

"Raphinha is a real wind-up merchant," Cotterill laughs. "He's in the faces of the opposition and the referees. But if he can control himself, he's a leading light."

As for Brazil's 'next big thing,' the hype is centred on Chelsea's Estevao - who, unfortunately for Ancelotti and Co. looks set to miss the tournament after picking up a serious hamstring injury in the Blues' 1-0 defeat to Manchester United this month.

But whether or not we see Estevao in North America this summer, Cotterill believes the sky is the limit for the teenager. "I've spoken to many scouts here in Brazil and they've always said that Estevao has no ceiling," Cotterill says. "There are no limits on what he can achieve. He's got the pace, he's got the balance, he has belief, he's a problem solver.

‌



"He can find ways of getting around the opposition. But he's only going to be 19 in April, still very young. And I don't think he's at that level - yet - to carry Brazil on a regular basis."

View 5 Images Estevao is the next big thing of Brazilian football (Image: Getty Images)

The Ancelotti gamble

The appointment of Carlo Ancelotti is the ultimate "win or bust" move. While the Italian is popular with the media, the pressure of being the first foreign boss in the modern era is immense.

"There is still resistance to having foreign coaches here," Cotterill notes. "If he wins, it's fantastic. If he loses, he's going to get thrown under the bus. Brazil will likely cruise the group stages - they always do - but as soon as they hit a half-decent European side, they've crashed out for 20 years.

‌



"Ancelotti's job isn't tactics; i t's more about managing the personnel because you've got so many fantastic players. His problem will be finding the right blend of who to bring in at the right time."

View 5 Images Carlo Ancelotti is under pressure to perform (Image: Getty Images)

Pressure and past trauma

In Brazil, the pressure to secure a sixth star isn't just sporting; it's cultural. To understand the Brazilian psyche, one must understand that the trauma of their 7-1 semi-final drubbing by Germany in 2014 never truly left. In fact, it changed the way the country speaks.

‌



"The phrase in Portuguese now is: 'Every day is a 7-1,'" Cotterill reveals. "If you've got many problems, that's how you describe it. In 1950, when they lost the final to Uruguay, few people actually saw it. But in 2014, millions saw it worldwide. It was a hammer blow."

This lingering scar has created a "win-at-all-costs" mentality that leaves no room for silver medals - and a mantra for the nation to live by. "It's like Ayrton Senna, the Formula 1 legend, used to say: finishing second is just being the first of the losers," Cotterill explains. "That is the attitude here. Anything less than winning the trophy is considered a total failure."

While every major footballing nation carries baggage, Brazil's burden is uniquely psychological. We saw the cracks at their home World Cup of 2014 when players were reduced to tears during the national anthem. "In 2014, the pressure was amplified, and even experienced players could not cope. They let their emotions get to them," says Cotterill.

"Nowadays, they have psychologists and a full backroom staff to help them use those emotions positively. They'll need it, because the fans don't care about the 'Beautiful Game' anymore - if they park the bus and win, the country will be ecstatic."

‌



Expectations

On paper, Brazil's path through the opening round looks relatively smooth. They find themselves in a group alongside Morocco, Haiti and Scotland. While those fixtures might provide some 'banana skin' potential for others, Cotterill expects the usual script to play out - at least initially.

"It's going to be the same old, same old," he predicts. "Brazil have become rather predictable over the last 20 years. They'll cruise through the group stage - or they should do - and probably through the next phase too. But the major problem is that as soon as they come up against any half-decent side, they crash out."

For a generation of Brazilian players, European opposition has become a mental block. "In the last 20 years, they've consistently gone out to European sides," Cotterill notes. "I remember one of the defenders complaining that there were too many European teams in the tournament!

‌



"They'll navigate the early phases with ease but the real test is whether Ancelotti can stop the rot when they meet the heavy hitters in the business end of the summer."

Sports.title: Coventry City chairman speaks out on Frank Lampard to Chelsea talk after brutal sack
Sports.content:
Coventry City chairman speaks out on Frank Lampard to Chelsea talk after brutal sack

Frank Lampard has been linked with a third return to Chelsea after leading Coventry City to the Championship title

View 2 Images Frank Lampard has led Coventry City to the Championship title - and the club's chairman has spoken about his future (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Coventry City owner Doug King has said that Frank Lampard found a ‘happy place’ with the club after leading them to promotion. The Sky Blues manager has been linked with Premier League clubs over the last few weeks after his success in the Championship.

‌



The latest link is a return to Chelsea, where the midfielder spent the majority of his glittering playing career and has been manager twice. The Blues announced the sacking of Liam Rosenior on Wednesday after just three months.

‌



The decision came after Chelsea lost their fifth Premier League game in a row, 3-0 to Brighton on Tuesday night, leaving them in eighth place in the Premier League table.

‌



Jurgen Klopp's stance on Chelsea job clear after Liam Rosenior sacked READ MORE :

There’s no surprise, given his links to the club, tthat there has been some talk about Lampard making a move to Chelsea. King, though, appears relaxed about the situation.

Speaking to BBC CWR , he said: "He's done a fantastic job, it's been an incredible 18 months for us and for him. I am sure he's in reflective mode. I said to him 'do not underestimate how difficult what you've just achieved is to do'.

"He's done huge things in his playing career but to get out of this league as champions without a parachute payment, from where we've come from, is a huge achievement nobody can take away from him.

‌



FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Everybody is going to get linked with everything, it's a merry-go-round. It's a bit disappointing clubs are appointing three or four managers a season.

"We don't want to be in those positions, that means something has gone a little bit astray."

‌



Coventry confirmed their place at the top of the Championship on Tuesday night with a 5-1 win over Portsmouth. Celebrations will now continue for the remaining two league games, with Lampard at the centre.

View 2 Images Coventry City owner Doug King spoken out about speculation surrounding Frank Lampard (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

King added: "You can see how emotionally connected (Lampard) is with the city, you can see what it meant to him to get promotion and then the title and I think he's found a happy place at the moment.

Article continues below

"It doesn't mean there's not going to be some staggering bid for him in the summer and he'll have to make his choices, because he's shown his credentials as a high quality head coach, but I'm not going to comment on that, I can't control it.

"I just think he's happy, I'm happy, everybody's happy, we've just got smiles on our faces and we don't worry about what may or may not happen for the head coach."

Sports.title: Inside Liverpool's final decision on Arne Slot future and what must come next at Anfield
Sports.content:
Inside Liverpool's final decision on Arne Slot future and what must come next at Anfield

Liverpool owners, Fenway Sports Group will stick with manager Arne Slot even though he has endured a difficult season in the defence of his Premier League title

View 3 Images It now seems almost certain Arne Slot will be in charge of Liverpool next season (Image: Getty Images)

If Liverpool beat Crystal Palace at Anfield in their next Premier League game, they will have an eight-point cushion to sixth spot and, with four fixtures to fulfil, can be almost sure of playing in next season’s Champions League. But Arne Slot might well have another target.

‌



If his team wins all five of their remaining matches, the Dutchman will have finish - points-wise - with a better title defence than Jurgen Klopp made in 2020-21. After winning his one and only Premier League in 2019-20, with an astonishing 99 points, Klopp amassed only 69 points the following season.

‌



If Slot’s Liverpool win their last five games, they will finish on 70 points. And when Liverpool’s hierarchy have been pondering Slot’s position, that 2020-21 season will have been a factor, for sure.

‌



Michael Edwards, now the chief executive of football at the club, was then Liverpool’s director of football. In that 2020-21 season, Liverpool were knocked out of the FA Cup in the fourth round by Manchester United and out of the Champions League quarter-finals by Real Madrid.

Juventus issue Mo Salah transfer statement with Liverpool exit just weeks away READ MORE :

This season’s FA Cup loss to Manchester City came at the quarter-final stage and the Champions League exit to Paris Saint-Germain at the quarter-final stage. In the Premier League, Liverpool have more points now after 33 games (55 in fifth position) than Klopp’s side did after 33 games of the 2020-21 season (54 in fifth position).

The Liverpool hierarchy know how difficult the season following a Premier League triumph can be, even if Pep Guardiola made it look easy. The caveat to Klopp’s title defence - compared with Slot’s - is that he did not welcome an influx of summer signings that cost in excess of £400million.

‌



But Edwards and Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s sporting director, recognise the sometimes chronic issues the expensive recruits have had in settling into life at the club. Most of those issues have been physical. Alexander Isak, now recovered from a broken leg, has missed 145 days of the season.

View 3 Images Alexander Isak has missed a huge chunk of his first season at Liverpool through injury (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Jeremie Frimpong has missed 117 days of the season with hamstring problems. Hugo Ekitike is now out long-term, probably not making his comeback from a ruptured achilles until 2027.

‌



And while Florian Wirtz has only missed a couple of weeks with injury, he has clearly taken time to adapt to the more robust demands of the Premier League. These problems will have been taken into account by Edwards, Hughes and the Fenway Sports Group when assessing the season. And, of course, there is the unquantifiable impact of the tragic passing of Diogo Jota.

When it looked as though Liverpool would face a real fight for a Champions League place, Slot’s position was under threat, no doubt. But in the extremely unlikely event they do not finish in the top five, he could still be safe. To win the Premier League in your first season in English football gives you a lot of credit.

And Slot deserves a third season. A perfect storm of things has gone wrong in his title defence - among them, Mo Salah’s prolonged dip in form - and he will know how to go about rectifying things.

‌



View 3 Images Arne Slot has yet to get the best out of Florian Wirtz (Image: PA)

The squad needs strengthening in the full-back areas and an alternative to Salah will be found in the transfer market. And Slot has a good squad at his disposal already. Rio Ngumoha must be given a key role next season. He can reinvigorate this Liverpool attack.

After Klopp’s tame title defence in 2020-21, the German delivered the 2021-22 FA Cup, the 2021-22 EFL Cup, a second-placed finish in the 2021-22 Premier League - with 92 points and only two defeats - and a runners-up finish in the Champions League. That was some season.

Article continues below

It will be a tall order for Slot to replicate that. But on the basis of recent history, it is right he is given the chance.

Sports.title: Man Utd can sign ideal Casemiro replacement for cut-price transfer fee
Sports.content:
Man Utd can sign ideal Casemiro replacement for cut-price transfer fee

Manchester United are looking for midfielders ahead of the summer transfer market as Casemiro is set to leave the club

View 2 Images Casemiro is set to leave Manchester United at the end of the season (Image: Izzy Poles - AMA, Getty Images)

Manchester United have already earmarked Wolves star Joao Gomes as a potential bargain signing in their pursuit of midfield reinforcements. The club face the task of finding a replacement for Casemiro this summer, with a wider midfield overhaul also expected at Old Trafford.

‌



Brazil captain Casemiro has been pivotal to the team's revival under Michael Carrick, which has pushed the club to the brink of securing a Champions League place. The 34-year-old has been a near ever-present throughout the campaign and has remarkably netted eight league goals from defensive midfield.

‌



It was confirmed in January that the former Real Madrid stalwart would be departing Old Trafford at the end of the season. United have since shown interest in a number of midfielders, with Casemiro's fellow Brazilian Gomes among them.

‌



The Manchester Evening News reported in March that the Wolves midfielder was being monitored by United ahead of the summer window. Despite the West Midlands club's ill-fated season, his displays have attracted the attention of United and several other Premier League sides.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Gomes, who has featured 31 times in the league this season, has previously attracted interest from top clubs but could now be signed for a reduced transfer fee following his side's confirmed drop to the second tier. While he has several years left on his contract, Wolves are expected to offload some of their most prized assets after relegation to the Championship.

‌



Man Utd ready to rival Liverpool in transfer race for Tottenham star Micky van de Ven READ MORE :

The 25-year-old has spent three years in English football since arriving as a highly-regarded talent from Flamengo. Gomes' performances earned him a Brazil call-up and he has won 10 caps for his country.

It promises to be a crucial summer for United as they seek to appoint a permanent manager and build upon their recent return to Champions League qualification. Beyond replacing Casemiro, the Manchester Evening News reported that the club aim to bring in two midfielders, with Manuel Ugarte expected to leave after a challenging two-year stint.

United have explored Nottingham Forest's Elliot Anderson as a potential option, though the England international is reportedly close to joining Manchester City. The club also maintain interest in Brighton's Carlos Baleba, despite his recent loss of form, and Crystal Palace star Adam Wharton.

‌



View 2 Images Wolves midfielder Joao Gomes has attracted interest from Manchester United (Image: Gareth Copley/Getty Images)

Meanwhile, Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Newcastle United star Sandro Tonali have also been considered. While all of the aforementioned players boast Premier League experience, Gomes would arguably command the lowest transfer fee following Wolves' relegation, which was confirmed after West Ham's draw with Palace on Monday.

As United weigh up their transfer options, finding a replacement for Casemiro in the heart of midfield will prove no small feat. Having played in the same position during his own career, Carrick has previously spoken about the Brazilian's significance to his side.

‌



"Yeah, well, listen, it's an important position," the United boss said in February. "Not being biased, obviously, as being a midfielder, but I think it is an important position to try and tie everything together and you're connected to the whole team, and that's sometimes emotionally, a little bit mentally, and showing that composure and understanding of the game a little bit.

"Case has had a big influence within the group on that. So, something we're fully aware of moving forward, for sure," he added, noting how getting his replacement right will be crucial."

Sports.title: Michael Owen's daughter to follow in dad's sporting footsteps and admits she's 'been humbled'
Sports.content:
Michael Owen's daughter to follow in dad's sporting footsteps and admits she's 'been humbled'

The daughter of ex-Liverpool and Manchester United star Michael Owen is set to follow in his footsteps as she prepares to make a sporting debut

View 3 Images Michael Owen will soon see his daughter Gemma Owen ride at Goodwood (Image: PA)

Michael Owen's daughter Gemma is preparing to make her debut as a jockey in the Markel Magnolia Cup on Ladies' Day at Goodwood. Her England legend father also took part in a charity race back in 2017 at Ascot.

‌



The 22-year-old shot to fame on season eight of Love Island UK in 2022 and is equally an accomplished dressage rider who has proudly represented Great Britain, having competed since the age of 11.

‌



Former Liverpool and Manchester United star Michael also shares a deep passion for horses, having founded Manor House Stables in 2006. He is currently collaborating with Classic-winning trainer Hugo Palmer on the Flat and his yard is home to over 140 horses, including his daughter's dressage competitors.

‌



The pair will cross disciplines in July, however, when Gemma mounts a racehorse and takes part in an all-female jockey charity race. While Gemma is well-versed in dressage, the sheer pace of the track will be an entirely new challenge, and like all her fellow competitors, she will be undergoing rigorous training in preparation.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Michael Owen makes Premier League 1-2-3-4-5-6 prediction with shock inclusion READ MORE :

The Markel Magnolia Cup is scheduled for July 30 at Goodwood Racecourse in Sussex. In the 15 years since it was first established, the event has raised an impressive £3.5million for charities dedicated to supporting women and children.

‌



View 3 Images The Love Island star will take to the track in July (Image: Goodwood Racecourse)

All participants, including Gemma, will receive instruction at the British Racing School ahead of the event. The TV star has been working alongside retired jockey Franny Norton.

Gemma's father has previously completed a comparable challenge, riding Calder Prince at Ascot nine years ago, coming second in The Prince's Countryside Fund Charity Race.

‌



Discussing her upcoming jockey debut, Gemma said: "I'm really looking forward to taking part in the Markel Magnolia Cup this year. Believe it or not, I had never sat on a racehorse until a couple of months ago and the training so far has been humbling to say the least.

"Spending more time at Manor House Stables, seeing how a racing yard runs like clockwork and getting out onto the gallops, has been an incredible experience.

View 3 Images Gemma is a seasoned dressage rider (Image: Goodwood Racecourse)

‌



"It is an even bigger challenge than I initially expected but I'm excited to take part in such a prestigious fundraising event which raises so much money for charities supporting women and children."

Gemma will be hoping for as thrilling a ride as her father enjoyed in 2017, who delivered a glowing assessment after the race. Michael said: "I love it, it was better than I expected.

"It went really quick early on. That was probably the fastest I've ever been on a horse. It was a long straight and I got very tired on the last furlong. I'm a million miles away. I'm making a start and considering I've only sat on a horse for the first time six months ago, I'm chuffed."

Sports.title: Luke Littler joins forces with Michael Owen and Stephen Bunting to buy £54k racehorse
Sports.content:
Luke Littler joins forces with Michael Owen and Stephen Bunting to buy £54k racehorse

Darts stars Luke Littler and Stephen Bunting have partnered with England and Liverpool legend Michael Owen and bought a racehorse

View 3 Images Luke Littler has chosen to dip his toes into horse ownership (Image: Getty)

Luke Littler and Stephen Bunting are now racehorse owners after joining forces with Michael Owen. The two-year-old colt in question is aptly named Bunting Mental.

‌



Reigning PDC world champion Littler is used to duelling with Bunting on the Premier League oche but the darting duo have come together to purchase a horse with former Liverpool and Manchester United striker Owen.

‌



Bunting Mental is trained by Cheshire-based handler Hugo Palmer, who has been operating out of Owen's Manor House Stables since 2022. The ex-England man founded the base in 2006 and began operating in 2007, dedicating much of his time to racing since his 2013 retirement.

‌



Littler was spotted at the Cheltenham Festival in March, enjoying proceedings with his girlfriend Faith Millar. He and Bunting have evidently been inspired to dive into ownership.

Sports.title: FIFA issue immediate response to calls for Italy to replace Iran at the World Cup
Sports.content:
FIFA issue immediate response to calls for Italy to replace Iran at the World Cup

An envoy to US President Donald Trump has suggested that Iran be replaced by Italy at the World Cup in North America this summer and now governing body FIFA have responded

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino wants Iran to play at the World Cup (Image: Alex Wong/Getty Images)

FIFA have no intention of replacing Iran with Italy at the World Cup this summer after one of Donald Trump's envoys suggested the controversial move. Iran's presence at the tournament will be awkward for Trump amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, but the United States President has no authority to stop them playing.

‌



Trump has previously said it would not be "appropriate" for the Iranians to compete "for their own life and safety". His hard line stance comes with the US and Israel still at war with Iran, despite a ceasefire currently being in place.

‌



The World Cup kicks off on June 11 and takes place across the US, Canada and Mexico. Iran qualified for the 48-team tournament and are scheduled to play in Group G against New Zealand and Belgium in Los Angeles and against Egypt in Seattle.

‌



However, with just 49 days to go until the World Cup begins, US special envoy Paolo Zampolli floated the idea of swapping Iran for Italy. The Italians will not be at the World Cup for the third straight occasion after losing to Boznia and Herzegovina in a play-off on March 31.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Bruno Fernandes discovers transfer fate as Man Utd change mind over summer sale READ MORE :

Donald Trump aide wants Italy at 2026 World Cup and names team they can replace READ MORE :

There won't be a reprieve for the Azzurri, with BBC Sport reporting that FIFA have not given any thought into such a move. World football's governing body have pointed to recent remarks by president Gianni Infantino where he said: "The Iranian team is coming, for sure."

‌



Zampolli's suggestion, in an interview with the Financial Times, was reportedly born out of a desire to repair relations between the US and Italy following tensions. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni had criticised Trump over his comments towards Pope Leo XIV.

But ultimately it is FIFA who hold the power to make decisions over the World Cup and, despite being a close ally of Trump, Infantino has repeatedly waved away suggestions of changes towards Iran. He has previously rejected calls for Iran's fixtures to be moved from the west coast of the US to Mexico and has reassured the country of FIFA's stance.

View 2 Images Iran will be at the World Cup (Image: (Photo by Gao Meng/VCG via Getty Images))

‌



“We want Iran to play, and Iran will play at the World Cup. There is no plan B, C or D – there is only plan A. Iran represent their people – both those living in Iran and those living abroad," he said last month after flying to Turkey to watch Iran play Costa Rica in a friendly.

“Iran will be at the FIFA World Cup, and we’re excited because they’re a very, very strong team, in my opinion, right now. So, I’m very happy. I’ve seen the team, I’ve spoken to the players and the coach. So, everything’s fine. We’re delighted because they are a very, very strong team. I’m very happy.”
